root_idea.summary: The root has two principal semantic axes: dust or earth, and equality or being of the same age.
root_idea.development: The dust axis yields meanings involving becoming dusty, poverty through clinging to the earth, wealth likened to the quantity of dust, and dust-bearing conditions. The equality axis yields peers or coevals and anatomical terms associated with aligned chest bones.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic form is the plural أَتْرَاب, normalized under its directly attested singular citation form تِرْب.
Independent Quran-attested noun for poverty or need.
Independent Quran-attested noun meaning dust or earth.
The Quranic plural تَرَائِب is normalized under the directly attested singular citation form تَرِيبَة.

senses.definition: A peer, coeval, or equal in age and standing; a well-matched counterpart.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is plural أَتْرَاب. It describes persons matched in age or likeness, including the women described in the Quranic passages, while the lexical term itself can be applied more broadly to male or female peers.

senses.definition: Poverty or need that leaves a person clinging to the dust or earth.
senses.usage_conditions: A conventional abstract noun for severe poverty, especially in the Quranic expression ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ, one reduced to contact with the earth through want.

senses.definition: Dust or earth, especially the fine particles or material of the ground.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran uses the noun for earthly material in creation, human origin, resurrection imagery, and comparisons or parables. It can refer generally to earth as well as to dry dust.

senses.definition: The upper chest or breast area, including its bones or ribs.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is the plural تَرَائِب in the expression between the ṣulb and the tarāʾib. Lexical descriptions variously delimit the term as the upper breast, the chest bones, the area near the collarbones, or ribs of the chest; these are related descriptions of the same anatomical region.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become dusted or dusty; of a place, to abound in dust or earth; to have dust on or in the hand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verb describing contact with or an abundance of dust.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become poor, needy, or reduced to clinging to the dust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The poverty sense is explained through the image of having nothing between oneself and the earth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become wealthy, with abundant possessions likened to the quantity of dust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This contrary wealth sense is attested alongside the poverty sense; the wealth interpretation is reported as the more familiar one in the lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An imprecatory or exhortatory expression wishing failure, loss, or contact with the dust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may be used conventionally without an intended literal imprecation, including as an emphatic incitement or reproach.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Association or consorting among peers or equals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun formed from the relation of people who are تِرْب, matched companions or coevals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put or sprinkle dust or earth upon something; to dust, soil, or treat an object with dust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may concern an ordinary object, a writing sprinkled with dust to dry its ink, or a hide treated with dust in preparation for use; the intensive form can indicate applying much dust or damaging an object with it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To possess a slave who has previously been possessed three times.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare specialized lexical use distinct from the dust-related causative sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become defiled or soiled in or with dust or earth; to have dust adhering to it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive or reflexive Form V use describing an object's becoming dust-covered.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dusty, dust-covered, or carrying dust; of a wind, bringing or driving along dust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to places, soil, food, flesh, and dust-bearing winds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Poor, needy, or cleaving to the dust through want.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective describing a person reduced to poverty or need.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A grave, burial place, cemetery, or the earth associated with a grave.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use distinct from the ordinary material sense of dust or earth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The end joint of a finger, the part in which the nail lies.
A plant of the plains or soft ground, described as having serrated leaves and, in one account, a purgative effect on camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The botanical identification is described variously in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Submissive or tractable, especially of a camel; readily manageable or easy to lead.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to male or female camels and, by extension in the lexical explanation, to land or other things that are easy to traverse or manage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In idiomatic or imprecatory expressions, dust or earth can signify poverty, disappointment, nothingness, or the grave.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Expressions such as having dust as one's lot or dust in one's mouth carry figurative meanings beyond the material noun, including wishing loss or alluding to death and burial.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Possessing much wealth; rich and without want.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The wealth sense is the more familiar of the two contrary senses reported for this adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having little wealth or being poor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A contrary, less familiar sense is also attested for the same adjective.

cautions: أَتْرَاب and تَرَائِب are Quranic plural forms; the public headwords are normalized to their directly attested singular citation forms تِرْب and تَرِيبَة.
The anatomical scope of تَرَائِب varies in classical descriptions between the upper chest, breast or chest bones, the collarbone region, and ribs.
The derivatives تَرِبَ and مُتْرِب are reported with contrary poverty and wealth senses; the artifact preserves both rather than collapsing them.
